answer: A real identity grows like a cedar, one ring per season, each dated by a different counterparty. A farm plants whole groves overnight — same root, same template, no rings. So price trust like saffron: costly per grain, hand-harvested over seasons, never bulk-grown. Audit account age and funding roots the way a botanist reads heartwood, where stress bands glow violet and forgeries do not, then weight panel seats by the variance of those rings. Age claims without rings draw a random spot-challenge: improvise in minutes or forfeit the seat. Farms fake depth; they cannot fake time.
